prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 1997 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and approach
- New Labour promises national renewal: prosperity with social justice, “for the many, not the few.”
- Pragmatic, non‑ideological: “what counts is what works.” Commitments are specific and measurable.

Core commitments over five years
- Education first; no rise in basic or top income tax; stable, low-inflation growth; NHS rebuilt; tough on crime and its causes; modern welfare; environmental protection and integrated transport; cleaner politics with decentralisation; leadership in Europe.

Education and skills
- Cut class sizes to 30 or under for ages 5–7 by ending the Assisted Places Scheme; nursery places for all four-year-olds.
- Raise standards: focus on literacy/numeracy, setting by ability, baseline assessment, action on failing schools.
- Wire schools to the internet (National Grid for Learning); invest in teacher IT skills.
- Strengthen teacher quality (induction year, General Teaching Council, headship qualification).
- Lifelong learning: University for Industry; Individual Learning Accounts; broader A-levels and stronger vocational routes.
- Higher education: income-contingent graduate repayments; fairer administration.

Economy and tax
- Stability first: low inflation (2.5% target), reform Bank of England for depoliticised monetary policy.
- Fiscal rules: borrow to invest, not for current spend; debt kept prudent.
- No increase in basic/top income tax; aim for 10p starting rate; cut VAT on fuel to 5%; no VAT on essentials.
- First two years within existing spending limits; comprehensive spending review; “save to invest.”
- Promote savings/investment (ISAs, corporate and CGT review).
- Welfare-to-work Budget funded by a windfall levy on privatised utilities.

Business, jobs and work
- Tougher competition law; smarter, faster Private Finance Initiative.
- Back small firms (cut red tape, statutory interest on late payment, better advice/exports); create Regional Development Agencies.
- Invest in science/technology; drive green industries and renewables.
- Keep key 1980s union laws; introduce a sensibly set National Minimum Wage via a Low Pay Commission; union recognition where majority support; encourage employee ownership; sign the EU Social Chapter.

Welfare to work
- 250,000 under-25s into work/training via four options (private, voluntary, study, environment taskforce), with rights and responsibilities.
- Replace failed youth schemes; incentives to hire the long-term unemployed; proactive help for lone parents; crack down on fraud.

NHS and public health
- End the internal market; shift admin savings to care (first £100m funds 100,000 extra treatments); end waits for cancer surgery.
- Primary care groups, multi‑year hospital agreements, outcome‑based quality standards; more real-terms funding yearly.
- Ban tobacco advertising; independent Food Standards Agency.

Crime and communities
- Halve time from arrest to sentence for persistent young offenders; final warning replaces repeat cautions; Youth Offender Teams.
- Reform CPS (decentralise); clearer sentencing and tougher for serious repeat offenders.
- Zero tolerance of disorder; parental responsibility orders; new offences for racial harassment; anti‑drugs coordinator; free vote to ban all handguns; more police on the beat.

Families, housing, pensions, care
- National childcare strategy; basic worker protections (limits on excessive hours, holidays, unpaid parental leave); protect and uprate Child Benefit.
- Protect homeowners (fair mortgages, anti‑gazumping); reinvest council house receipts to build/repair; duty to house homeless families.
- Keep basic state pension (uprate with prices), retain SERPS option; create stakeholder pensions; Royal Commission on long-term care.

Environment, transport, culture
- Every department “green”; integrated transport policy; stronger rail regulation and new rail authority; PPP for London Underground; roads review; protect rural services; animal welfare measures and access to countryside.
- NESTA to back young talent; protect school playing fields; fairer lottery distribution with not‑for‑profit operator; support 2006 World Cup bid.

Clean politics and constitution
- End hereditary peers’ voting rights; party funding transparency and ban foreign donations; Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the ECHR into UK law.
- Devolution via referendums: Scottish Parliament, Welsh Assembly; London mayor/authority; modernise Commons; stronger, accountable local government; possible English regional assemblies by consent.

Europe and the world
- Lead EU reform/enlargement; sign Social Chapter; keep veto on key areas; decide on the euro by economic test with a referendum.
- Defence through NATO; retain Trident; strategic review; stronger arms control and landmine ban; responsible arms exports.
- New Department for International Development; refocus aid on poverty, move toward 0.7% UN target; champion human rights and climate action (CO2 –20% by 2010).

Five election pledges
- Smaller infant classes; fast-track youth justice; cut NHS waiting lists by 100,000 via red-tape savings; 250,000 young people into work via windfall levy; no rise in income tax rates, cut VAT on heating to 5%, keep inflation/interest low.
